text.p: Persistent tight liquidity in the Turkish market since last Friday prompted heavy central bank funding on Thursday, bankers said.
But the bond market was on the buying side which produced a fall of around 1.5 percentage points in yields and overnight repo rates.

The central bank lent 20.5 trillion lira at 72 percent overnight and also funded the banks a total of 45.6 trillion lira on tomorrow/next and tomorrow/week forward swaps at 67 and 68 percent, respectively.
The average overnight money rate rose slightly to 71.92 percent from 71.12 on Wednesday.
Bond yields dropped to 91 percent levels from around 93 percent on Wednesday amid demand which emerged due to the market's attempts to test levels just below the 90 percent mark, bankers said.

"The market met strong resistance at 94 percent levels on Wednesday which signalled that yields would test lower levels at just below 90 percent. Capital gains is taken into consideration rather than the cost of funding," a banker said.
The most actively traded paper was December 10, 1997 which yielded 91.63 percent, down 1.57 percent. The second active one was April 22, 1998 at 93.22 percent, down 0.33 percent.
The average overnight repo dropped, on bond demand, by around a point to 71.41 percent on Thursday.
Turkish lira firmed against the dollar by rising to 125,260 from the close at 125,400 on Wednesday in line with mark strength against the dollar.
